title: Invention fact cards
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: Victorian Britain and the Industrial Revolution (Revolution)
source: Seeded from history/y6 lesson 22 (Invention fact cards (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 22: Victorian inventions and their legacy. To understand which Victorian inventions changed life and how they still affect us

cards:
invention
a new thing someone creates

legacy
something left for the future

Great Exhibition
a show of inventions from
around the world in 1851
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: Which invention let anyone send a letter for a penny?
questions.model: Before 1840 the receiver paid by distance. Then a stamp cost one penny. That stamp was the Penny Black.

questions.q: Where was the Crystal Palace first built?
Give one Victorian invention we still use.
questions.a: Stamps, postboxes, telephones, light bulbs, sewers, railways

questions.q: Make an invention fact card for three inventions (date, what it did, impact then, legacy now).
questions.a: Three accurate cards with impact and legacy
questions.model: Teacher completes the Penny Black card.

questions.q: Compare a Victorian and modern railway map: one change and one continuity.
questions.a: Change: some lines closed; continuity: main lines still run

questions.q: Muslim scholars like Ibn al-Haytham studied light centuries earlier. How does knowledge build over time?
questions.a: Each age builds on earlier discoveries, like optics leading to lenses and cameras

questions.q: Big question: which invention could you not live without?
questions.a: A reasoned choice using impact and legacy
